section: Adjoining end side panel for N_Elle
source_pages: printed p.444-445 / PDF 446-447, both pages read whole 2026-08-26
extraction_note: Taken with the Maxima pages on 2026-08-26 so that the collection question stops blocking work. WHICH COLLECTION THIS KITCHEN IS remains open - the glass row's page carries an N_Elle mark while the estimate header says MAXIMA 2.2 (see glass_wall_h96.json collection_note) - and holding all three files means the answer changes a picker choice and not an extraction.
height_note: ONLY THREE HEIGHTS: 36,8 / 78 / 84. Not a subset of the Maxima table - 36,8 is a height that appears nowhere in the Maxima panel pages, and it is the same 36,8 the N_Elle fillers use on printed p.435. A different collection is a different height grammar.
band_note: Bands 1-4 are '-' on every row, and band 11 carries a price where the Maxima pages print '-'. The band set is a property of the collection, not of the panel.
depth_note: EVERY GROUP PRINTS TWO NUMBERS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER. The label names the CARCASS depth the panel serves ('for 35-cm deep side panel + door thickness'); the 'd.' beside it is the depth the catalog DRAWS. Across all eight groups in this chapter the second is the first plus 2,2 per door face, rounded up - 35 -> 37,2 -> d.37,5; 70 -> 74,4 -> d.75; 124 -> 128,4 -> d.129. That arithmetic is DERIVED and is written here to explain the numbers, not to replace them: depth_mm below is the printed 'd.' verbatim. Whether 'd.' describes the finished end or the panel's own board is Elda Q21, and everything drawn at the end of a run depends on the answer.
label_collision_note: TWO GROUPS ON THIS PAGE CARRY THE SAME PRINTED LABEL. Both the d.102 and the d.107 group are printed 'for 62+35-cm deep side panel'. They cannot both be. The codes disagree with the label: at the heights where the letters are unambiguous the d.102 rows carry the prefixes this same chapter uses for a 62-deep panel and the d.107 rows carry the 67-deep prefixes, and the arithmetic in depth_note gives 62+35 -> 101,4 -> d.102 and 67+35 -> 106,4 -> d.107. The label is kept verbatim in printed_depth_label; the reading is Elda Q20. NOTE the letters are only a witness at the SHORT heights - from H.138 up, both groups use F-prefixes and are told apart by the trailing digits alone, which is rule 5 restated: a code is a lookup, never a decode.
extra_depth_note: This collection prints a group the Maxima pages do not: 'for 72+35-cm deep side panel', d.112. 72+35 = 107, plus two door faces = 111,4, rounded up = 112 - the same arithmetic as every other group, which is why it is worth recording that the rule survived a group it was not derived from.
surcharge_note: Printed beside these tables: vertical edge of door, 48 points up to H.72 and 65 from H.75 to H.140 (the 86-point band above H.141 is absent - this collection stops at H.84). And a charge the Maxima pages do not carry: 'Adjoining end side panel with 45 degree LIP in FENIX NT-NTM and UNICOLOR finishes from Cesar palette' - 205 points for 1 side and 205 for 2 sides, with the lip drawn at 23 mm. Both figures being 205 is what the page prints.

end_panel_45.description: Adjoining end side panel for N_Elle, 2.2 cm thick - with 45 degree vertical edge
end_panel_45.handed_note: The ARTICLE has no hand. A panel does not open, so there is no hinge to hand, and the catalog prints one code for either end of a run. What IS handed is the 45-degree edge, which must face the door - and that follows from which end you place it at, so it is placement and not an attribute. The choice the catalog DOES price is a different one: which page you are on. See the two unit types in this file.

front_layout.note: A PANEL HAS NO FRONT. 'none' is stated rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs defaults a missing layout to 'single' and would hang a door leaf on a flat board. A default is not a source.

end_panel_45_opposite_hinge.height_correction_2026_08_26: Y00129, the first row of the d.112 group, is PRINTED at H.84 and is recorded here at H.36,8. Two witnesses against the page: the parallel framed-door page (printed p.447) prints the identical group as 36,8 / 78 / 84, and Y0/Y3/Y6 is the prefix triple that means 36,8 / 78 / 84 in every other group of this collection - printed as 84 the group would hold two H.84 rows and no short one. Verified against the rendered page image, so this is the CATALOG's misprint and not a text-extraction artifact. The printed value is kept in printed_height_cm on that row.
